correctness.rationale: For every source load x and agent j the largest budget-feasible subset of x unit chores is min(x,b_j), so exact EF is precisely min(x,b_j)<=a_j. Any unsaturated agent must attain the maximal source load; all unsaturated loads coincide at t and all saturated loads are b_i<=t, yielding a_i=min(b_i,t), housekeeper h<=t, or the all-full case. The reverse implication is immediate. Distinct load vectors give the multinomial census. The adjacent feasible-workload bands have start gap R(t+1); the last nonempty gap occurs at t_* with R(t_*)>=t_*+1, since R is nonincreasing. This proves that F(t_*)-1 is impossible and all larger workloads are feasible. Exact independent direct-EF enumeration matched 6,066,226 assignments over 1206 parameter settings; the verifier checks 19525 heterogenous and 182 homogeneous capacity thresholds. No infinite conclusion is inferred solely from finite tests.

value.rationale: The homogeneous unit-size/unit-disutility case is a natural testbed for exact fairness under time budgets; the exact EF relation includes an unconstrained housekeeper. The result solves all load vectors and exact labeled allocation counts for every integer budget profile, and identifies the last impossible workload via a sharp strict-Durfee index. This gives a nontrivial capacity-dependent existence threshold with arithmetic gaps, not just a routine existence bound: e.g. four budget-five agents cannot process eleven unit chores exactly fairly, yet twelve chores have 369600 distinct EF assignments and every larger workload admits EF. The result is meaningful even without a broader heterogeneous-weight theorem.
